bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to set up women-only university, says CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar to set up women-only university, says CM Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced plans to establish a women-only university where faculty, students and non-teaching staff will all be women. He also highlighted government initiatives for women’s employment, education, entrepreneurship, healthcare and economic empowerment across the state By PTI Published Date - 28 August 2026, 12:00 AM Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said the state will have a ‘Mahila Vishwavidyalaya’, a university in which the faculty, students as well as non-teaching staff will all be women. He made the announcement at a function in the state capital where a sum of Rs 600 crore was disbursed among beneficiaries, through DBT, under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana which was rolled out last year. “I extend my greetings to all sisters of Bihar on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. We believe that the state can prosper only if our women do well… A Mahila Vishwavidyalaya will be set up in the state. The university will be run by women, from top to bottom. The vice chancellor, professors, other staffers and students shall all be women,” the chief minister said. The function was also marked by the signing of an MoU between the state’s Department for Excise and Prohibition and the Prajapita Brahma Kumari Ishwariya Vishwavidyalaya for spreading public awareness over the ills of consumption of intoxicants. Additionally, loans were also distributed among 10,000 beneficiaries from the JEEViKA Fund. Stressing that the government was committed to making women self-reliant and economically empowered, Choudhary said a target has been set to identify 10 lakh JEEViKA Didis and install solar panels at their homes by March 31 next year. JEEViKA Didis will also be associated with the deaddiction campaign to keep people away from intoxicants through street plays and other means, he added. The chief minister extended his best wishes to 7,376 women selected through the nurse recruitment examination conducted by the Bihar Public Service Commission, an official statement read. Choudhary highlighted that under the Chief Minister Balika PhD Fellowship, around 1,000 female students will receive financial assistance of Rs 10,000 per month for four years to pursue higher education and research — a decision that was announced by him on Wednesday. He lamented that there were only 600 women among 4,600 individuals pursuing PhD studies in Bihar. Follow Us : Tags Bihar Mahila Vishwavidyalaya Mukhyamantri Mahila Samrat Choudhary

national_raw_news.content: The death toll in the massive flash floods in Nepal today rose to 359 as authorities in Nepal race against time to find thousands of missing people, including 285 Indian tourists, in one of the country’s worst disasters in recent years. The flash floods yesterday wreaked havoc across three districts in Nepal. Nepal Police said that 93 more bodies were recovered today. According to Nepal Police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle, the bodies recovered so far include 108 in Chitwan, 62 in Nawalparasi East, 27 in Dhading, 20 in Gorkha, 17 in Rasuwa, 15 in Nawalparasi West, 12 in Nuwakot, and nine in Tanahun. Authorities in Tibet and Nepal have reported over 1,300 people missing as of today, out of these, many were foreigners. Both authorities reported that people from more than 30 countries are missing, mainly from India, the United States, Malaysia, Ukraine, Australia, Britain, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Germany and Russia. Nepal Police spokesperson Kafle said, over 800 stranded people, including those injured, have been rescued from the affected areas, so far. The flash floods were caused after an avalanche blocked the flow of the Lhende tributary of the Bhotekoshi and first hit Timure, near Nepal’s border with China at Rasuwagadhi.
